summary: Feed s165_triple to IDS is degraded: 20.5% one-way TCP sessions, VLAN 20 missing/stripped (45% untagged), and 75.8% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP conversations is reaching the IDS - likely SPAN/mirror configured for single direction or asymmetric routing without aggregation at the packet broker, so return traffic takes a different path and is not combined.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for stateful TCP reassembly and signature matching; 32 of 156 sessions are one-way, causing missed handshakes, broken stream reassembly, and evasion of detection.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow at the packet broker so the IDS sees client-to-server and server-to-client together for complete session reconstruction.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 traffic is not visible and 45% of packets are untagged - packet broker or SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags (e.g., trunk not preserved, port in access mode) so VLAN context is lost.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires VLANs [10, 20] for segmentation-aware detection; without VLAN 20 tags it cannot apply VLAN-specific policies and misses lateral movement or attacks inside VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Configure TAP/SPAN and packet broker to preserve and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 so IDS retains tenant/segment visibility.

findings.root_cause: 75.8% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) exceeding the IDS 60% tolerance - traffic is opaque without decryption, not a broker sampling issue.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection; high encryption blinds signature and anomaly detection, reducing coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective TLS decryption / visibility (e.g., decrypt mirror or key sharing) before the IDS or offload encrypted flows, to bring inspectable traffic within the IDS 60% encrypted-share budget.
